reasoning:
Country-level: The scene shows left-hand traffic with vehicles that are right-hand-drive, tropical vegetation, and a mix of compact MPVs common in Southeast Asia. The language on the small wall plaques appears Indonesian/Malay (e.g., “tinta”), pushing toward Indonesia over Malaysia because of the vehicle mix and urban design. Distinctive petal/solar-panel streetlights and stylized public-art panels along a pedestrian overpass are features seen in Jakarta after the 2018 Asian Games streetscape upgrades on the Sudirman–Thamrin corridor.
City-level: Jakarta specifically features the unique “solar flower” streetlights and renovated JPO (pedestrian bridges) with art panels along Jalan Jenderal Sudirman and near the Senayan/GBK (Gelora Bung Karno) green belt. The heavy tree cover next to multilane arterials and glimpses of a lone white tower block align with the Sudirman–Senayan area bordering GBK’s parklands. Other Indonesian cities (Bandung, Surabaya) lack this exact combination of street furniture and JPO design.
Street-level: The wall-mounted blue/white art panels and small inset windows belong to the revamped JPO structures near Senayan/GBK. The presence of the sculptural solar streetlight directly adjacent to the overpass and dense GBK treeline suggests the section around Bundaran Senayan/Polda Metro Jaya on Jalan Jenderal Sudirman, where traffic flows beside GBK’s perimeter and multiple JPOs with similar arches and art panels span the roadway. Exact pinpointing is difficult without a named sign, but the ensemble best fits the Sudirman–Senayan stretch near GBK.
